text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: Multiple private VNet peering sessions in Azure germanywestcentral are showing intermittent DNS resolution failures and asymmetric routing to on-prem via ExpressRoute. Affects Redwood Private customers in DE region. Paging primary on-call.

chris_oncall: saw the page, I'm looking. any customer reports yet? :eyes:

lucas_support: customer ticket #CS-9182 reports "Private API timeouts" from our DE on-prem integration. They've put a mitigation in place (local retry) but still seeing errors. I'll attach logs after.

maria_sre: chris, take primary, I'll pull routing/BGP. quick checks: control plane OK, API control endpoints healthy. Problem looks network-y.

chris_oncall: starting triage. first quick probe from one of our private nodes to customer on-prem gateway.

chris_oncall: ```
# from private-node-12 (germanywestcentral)
ping 10.11.5.1 -c 5
PING 10.11.5.1 (10.11.5.1): 56 data bytes
--- 10.11.5.1 ping statistics ---
5 packets transmitted, 3 received, 40% packet loss, time 4004ms
```

alex_net: running BGP summary on our ExpressRoute circuits and vnet-peerings now.

alex_net: ```
# bgp summary (egressedge1)
Neighbor        AS      MsgRcvd MsgSent  TblVer  InQ OutQ  Up/Down State/PfxRcd
10.21.0.2       65020   110233  110241   45     0    0   1:23:45  0
10.21.0.3       65021   3301    3299     23     0    0   0:02:12  1200
```

alex_net: noticing a mismatch: one of the eBGP peers (10.21.0.3) flapping routes to a subset of prefixes used by Private customers. Could be route reflector churn in the provider.

maria_sre: also seeing DNS lookup failures from internal resolvers to the delegated DNS zone for private endpoints. nslookup sometimes times out then works.

chris_oncall: ok hypothesis: provider-side route churn + intermittent DNS for private zones -> asymmetric flows causing tcp resets/timeouts.

kira_devex: are any hosted API customers impacted or only Private/VPC customers? We need to scope for public status page.

lucas_support: only Private/VPC customers reported so far (DE region ExpressRoute/Directconnect equivalents). No hosted API reports.

ingrid_prodsec: any customer data-plane retries in logs that look like encrypted traffic renegotiation? need to know for compliance notices.

maria_sre: I pulled tcp dumps from one of our edge boxes — seeing SYN then no ACKs sometimes, then later ACKs from different path. asymmetry confirmed.

chris_oncall: mitigation plan suggestion:
- move affected customers to alternate peering/region if they have active failover (customers with DR in netherlands/Frankfurt).
- temporarily enable prefix-specific static routes on our egress edge to prefer the stable peer (10.21.0.2) for the impacted prefixes.
- add DNS caching and increase retry backoff in private endpoint resolvers.

alex_net: I can push an ROI (route preference) for the impacted prefixes from egressedge1 -> prefer 10.21.0.2. Doing a dry-run then deploy.

alex_net: done dry-run, rolling change to prefer route via 10.21.0.2 now. monitoring BGP and flows.

incident-bot: Deploy job #deploy-5487 started by alex_net to update egress routing preferences. :gear:

chris_oncall: I'm updating customer comms with the mitigation steps and asking for permission to failover those with cross-region DR.

lucas_support: sent template to affected customers, adding one note: "we are enabling temporary static preference on our egress to stabilize routing; no action needed on your side unless we ask you to fail over." Customer response: :thumbsup: from 2 customers, one asked for ETA.

maria_sre: after the route preference change, BGP adjacency remained stable and packet loss dropped on the probes.

maria_sre: ```
# post-change probe
ping 10.11.5.1 -c 5
5 packets transmitted, 5 received, 0% packet loss
```

chris_oncall: DNS cache TTL lowered to 30s, added longer resolver retry loop. this should reduce transient lookup failures.

kira_devex: posting an incident channel note and preparing a short postmortem template. tagging infra and product.

ingrid_prodsec: documenting timeline; any chance this was a provider maintenance window? we need vendor SR numbers.

alex_net: opened SR#AZ-99834 with Azure networking; provider acknowledges intermittent route reflection problem and is investigating. They flagged a known issue in germanywestcentral interconnect fabric.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied. Route preference and DNS changes are active. Continue monitoring for 2 hours. If stable, we'll move to monitoring and begin RCA.

lucas_support: customers acknowledge; one asked for confirmation when fully resolved. I'll keep them updated.

maria_sre: handing off to night on-call @chris_oncall for watches. I'll be on-call for escalation until 22:00 CET then hand to next.

chris_oncall: taking watch. will check dashboards every 15m and watch BGP flaps. ping me in this thread if you see regressions.

kira_devex: scheduling postmortem doc in #product-operations. I'll own the customer impact section and timeline.

ingrid_prodsec: thanks all, ensure all changes are recorded in config repo and we have audit logs for route pref change. postmortem should capture mitigations and proposed hardening (more aggressive multi-path selection, DNS redundancy for private zones).

chris_oncall: logging final note before watch: temporary route pref will remain until Azure confirms fix or we push a permanent reroute. current state: stable.

incident-bot: thread auto-archiver scheduled in 7 days. Use /incident-close when RCA complete.
